introduction: On this Sunday, God speaks to Job from the storm and reminds him that he sets the limits of the sea. In the Gospel, a great storm strikes the boat while Jesus sleeps, and with a word he calms the wind and the waves. Paul tells us that the love of Christ urges us on, and that anyone in Christ is a new creation. Let us bring our storms to the Lord who is with us in the boat.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus is with us in every storm. Let us bring him our prayers with faith.
intentions: For the Church, tossed by many storms: that she may trust in the presence of the Lord who is always with her. Let us pray to the Lord.
For sailors, fishermen and all who work at sea, and for migrants crossing dangerous waters: that God may protect them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose lives are shaken by illness, loss or fear: that Christ may speak his word of peace to them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who feel that God is asleep or far away: that they may discover that he cares for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that the love of Christ may urge us to live no longer for ourselves but for him. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, you calmed the wind and the sea with a word. Be with us in every storm, increase our faith, and bring us safely to the other shore. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: Who then is this?
reflection.body:
Job has suffered terribly and has questioned God. When God finally answers, he speaks "out of the whirlwind" and asks who it was who set the boundaries of the sea and said, "You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here." The sea, for the people of the Bible, was a picture of chaos. Only God can master it.

In the Gospel, the disciples are crossing the lake at night when "A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat." Several of them are fishermen used to this lake, and still they are terrified. Jesus is asleep on a cushion in the stern. They wake him with a cry that many of us have prayed: "Teacher, don't you care that we are dying?"

Jesus gets up and speaks to the storm: "Peace! Be still!" And "The wind ceased and there was a great calm." Then he turns to them: "Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?" They are now afraid in a different way, and they ask the question Mark wants every reader to ask: "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?" The one who does what only God can do is in the boat with them.

Jesus does not promise that there will be no storms. He promises to be in the boat. Faith does not mean never being afraid; it means turning to him in our fear.

Paul tells us what moves a Christian: "For the love of Christ compels us." And he tells us what Christ makes of us: "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation." This week, name the storm you are facing, and bring it to Jesus in prayer. Then listen for his word of peace.
